question: Should yielded session rows keep `paused` while broader cron/run outcomes use `deferred`, or should both open PRs converge on one durable status name?
rationale: Both branches expose nonterminal yielded-parent state through persisted or public surfaces, and selecting that compatibility contract requires maintainer intent rather than code inference.

options.title: Separate projection layers
options.body: Keep `paused` for session rows and `deferred` for cron/run outcomes, documenting that they represent different lifecycle projections.

options.title: Unify status vocabulary
options.body: Choose one status name and align session persistence, Gateway, UI, cron, SDK, and docs before either branch lands.

options.title: Consolidate the branches
options.body: Pause both PRs until one shared parent-lifecycle design owns all yielded-session and yielded-run behavior.

recommendation.title: Separate projection layers
recommendation.body: Keep `paused` for session rows and `deferred` for cron/run outcomes, documenting that they represent different lifecycle projections.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the existing yielded-pause semantics and has recent ownership history in adjacent Gateway lifecycle code.
